This document is a writing-style profile of a person referred to as Jon Black, based on 1,777 chat messages and 55 ballot comments from a music league group, dated July 11 to August 30, 2026.

**Topics and references:** He mentions Conor (also called cjwookie) 148 times, more than any other group member; Sarah 52, Jensen 47, Matt 40, Mashew 23, Kozh 34, Clements 30, Shane 20, Jimmy 17, Palletz 13, Steiny 10. He frequently describes other members' behavior in third person as though documenting factual history. Recurring subject areas include league administration and rule enforcement, bathroom fixtures (particularly Toto bidets), his pets, and geographic/class comparisons between Reno, Bakersfield, Marin, and San Francisco. Musical interests he expresses include Guns N' Roses, Townes Van Zandt, NOFX, Lagwagon, Bob Dylan, and First Aid Kit, though he claims limited familiarity with most artists. Biographical details include UCLA, Sigma Chi, Peace Corps service in Kazakhstan, and Hastings law school. He is a lawyer but never uses the word.

**Mechanical habits:** Double space after periods (473 messages). Correct capitalization in long messages, lowercase in short ones (256 messages start lowercase). Occasional typos but consistently clean sentence structure. Double hyphen for em-dash (22 times). No "lol"; "haha" 23 times. 15 semicolons, mostly in numbered lists. Average message length 116 characters versus the group average of 85. High comma density (45 per 1,000 words) due to appositive phrases. Frequent sentence openers: "Also" (31), "I think" (22), "Well" (14). Only four emoji total. 30 exclamation points. All caps only for official announcements. No internet abbreviations. Average message burst of 1.39.

**Humor techniques:** Deadpan sarcasm (~40%), mock-legal or institutional register (~20%), extended character-assassination bits (~15%), absurd escalation

Writing style notes for this author:

- Uses curly apostrophes rather than straight ones.
- Rarely uses commas; substitutes spaced hyphens, periods, or nothing.
- Sends many short consecutive messages instead of one longer one, typically 5 to 15, escalating, with brief lines used as punchlines. Bursts are usually prompted by boredom, physical discomfort, alcohol, or catching up.
- Ends bursts with a false sign-off such as "Ok done" or "Ok bye guys," then continues.
- Frequently comments on the group chat itself: its volume, statistics, norms, social dynamics, and absent members.
- Claims participating is burdensome while posting more than others.
- Uses modifiers such as subtle, soft, hard, massive, anti.
- States things confidently without knowledge, then concedes readily when corrected.
- Occasionally uses an unusually advanced vocabulary word directed at one particular recipient, and notes that he is doing so.
- Tells stories in parts, delaying the conclusion, then reports it plainly, underselling the outcome so the anticlimax functions as the joke.
- Leaves typos uncorrected, then posts a correction prefixed with asterisks. Sometimes misspells a word badly and continues without fixing it.
- Refers to people by last name or nickname, one name per message; uses first names only when being sincere.
- Writes "ahah" instead of "haha" or "lol," and avoids emoji.
